YuvrajSingh

युवराज सिंह

Every planet in his chart is ordinary. What happened to him was not.

12 DEC 1981 · CHANDIGARH

TL;DR

Six sixes. Then six months to live.

Nothing in Yuvraj's chart is exalted. Nothing is debilitated. Not one planet sits in its own sign. On paper it is an unremarkable chart.
Which is exactly the point. His story was never about where the planets sat. It was about when each one took over.

His Jupiter era — the generous one — ran from 1996 to March 2012. Debut, six sixes, a World Cup, Player of the Tournament. Then it ended. Within weeks of that handover he was in a Boston hospital being told he had months.

The messy bits

Everything you're actually here for

He's remembered as the comeback story. The years around it were uglier than the highlight reel suggests. All public record.

🪨 The night they threw rocks at his house
What's public

2014 World T20 final, Dhaka. He made 11 off 21 balls in a chase India lost by six wickets.

A crowd gathered outside his Chandigarh home and pelted it with stones. Some in the crowd accused him of having taken money to underperform. No evidence was ever produced and no charge was ever brought. He said afterwards he had been very low on confidence and had actually been trying to get himself out.

What the chart hints

Two years into Saturn. Saturn is the planet of public weight — being made to carry something slowly, in front of everyone.

It's also the stretch that follows Jupiter, which is why it always feels like a punishment. It isn't. It's just the next one.

💰 ₹16 crore, and almost nothing to show
What's public

The 2015 IPL auction. Delhi Daredevils paid ₹16 crore for him — the most expensive player in the tournament's history at that point.

He scored 248 runs that season. The price became a punchline, and it followed him through the rest of his franchise career.

What the chart hints

Venus sits in Capricorn with Ketu. Venus is money and valuation; Capricorn is the sign that asks whether you've actually earned it.

Astrology doesn't set auction prices. But "valued highly, then audited" is a fair description of the placement.

🗣️ His father never stopped talking
What's public

Yograj Singh, a former India cricketer himself, has spoken repeatedly and publicly about how hard he pushed his son — and has given a long run of interviews attacking selectors, teammates and captains on Yuvraj's behalf.

Yuvraj has described a childhood built entirely around his father's ambition, including being made to give up the sport he actually preferred, which was roller skating.

What the chart hints

His Rahu stretch covers his entire childhood, to 1996. Rahu is hunger that doesn't originate with you — appetite you inherit and then carry.

The Sun, which stands for the father, sits in Scorpio: intense, controlling, hard to argue with.

🎯 Dropped. Recalled. Dropped again.
What's public

From 2012 onward he was in and out of the side constantly — never quite finished, never quite trusted. He played his last international in 2017 and only retired formally in 2019.

He has said openly that he felt he was never given a clean run after the illness, and that the uncertainty was harder than the chemotherapy.

What the chart hints

Textbook Saturn: delay, not denial. Saturn rarely closes a door. It leaves it open just far enough that you keep walking back to it.

Being straight with you: the match-fixing accusations shouted at his house in 2014 were exactly that — accusations from a crowd. Nothing was investigated, nothing was charged, and we repeat them only because the incident itself is the story. We are not using astrology to suggest anything about them.
Certified comeback arcs

He was told he had months

Player of the Tournament to chemotherapy in Boston

  • He was diagnosed with a mediastinal seminoma — a rare germ-cell tumour in the chest — not long after the 2011 World Cup he had just been the best player in.
  • He has said he was told he had three to six months. Three cycles of chemotherapy followed, in Boston and Indianapolis.
  • He was back in the India squad inside about a year, played the 2012 World T20, and won a man-of-the-match award in it.
  • He started the YouWeCan foundation for cancer patients the same year.

🔭 The chart bit: the Jupiter stretch closes in March 2012 and Saturn opens. Saturn is endurance — the capacity to keep going at reduced power for a long time. We are describing the timing of documented events. We are not suggesting the chart caused an illness, and nobody should.

Recalled at 35, and made his highest ODI score

  • By 2017 he had been written off for the second time. He was picked again almost as a courtesy.
  • He made 150 off 127 against England at Cuttack — the best one-day innings of his career, eight years after his peak.
  • He retired in 2019 with a World Cup, a World T20 and a remission.

🔭 The chart bit: five years into Saturn. Saturn rewards late, and only for time actually served.

Actually learn this

Astrology, but make it make sense

Zero background needed. Read this once and you can decode the chart above yourself — no astrologer required.

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

It's a photo of the sky from the exact spot and second you were born. Where each planet was sitting, frozen.

Vedic astrology says that snapshot describes the raw material you were handed — not your fate, your starting kit.

His: 12 December 1981, Chandigarh. Moon in Gemini, Sun in Scorpio, Mars and Saturn together in Virgo. Nothing dramatic — and that turns out to be the interesting part.
LESSON 02

Nine of them. Think of them as nine departments, each running one part of a life.

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters — and when it doesn't

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles.

  • Exalted — its best possible sign, running at full power.
  • Debilitated — its worst. Still works, just badly.
  • Own sign — home ground. Comfortable and reliable.
His scorecard: none of the above. Not one of his nine planets is exalted, debilitated or in its own sign. Every single one is somewhere in the middle. This is genuinely common — most charts look like this — and it is why the sign-by-sign approach tells you almost nothing about him. His story is in the timing instead, which is Lesson 04.
LESSON 04

Dashas — why timing is the whole game

This is the part most people have never heard of, and for Yuvraj it is the only part that matters.

Your life is split into long stretches, and each one is run by a single planet. The order is fixed, the lengths are fixed, and which one you start with is decided entirely by where the Moon was when you were born. The technical name is dasha.

His stretches, computed:
Rahu from birth to early 1996 · Jupiter 1996 to March 2012 · Saturn from March 2012

Now put the life next to it. Everything he is famous for sits inside Jupiter. The illness, the backlash and the long grind all sit inside Saturn. The handover is March 2012.
LESSON 05

Sub-periods — the chapters inside the chapter

A sixteen-year stretch is too blunt to be useful, so each one splits again into sub-periods, each handed to a different planet. That's how astrologers get from "this decade" to "this year".

Why we're not giving you his: sub-periods need the exact birth minute, and his recorded time is "12:00 noon" — a value round enough to be a placeholder rather than a record. The long stretches survive that doubt. The sub-periods would not.
LESSON 06

What we genuinely can't tell you

Here's where most celebrity astrology sites quietly cheat.

A chart has two halves. The signs, which we have and which barely move across a day. And the houses, which need the exact minute, because the rising sign changes about every two hours.

His time is recorded as noon at PGI Chandigarh. We tested every claim on this page across a six-hour window — 9am to 3pm — and all of them hold. His Moon stays in Gemini, stays in Ardra, and the era sequence doesn't move.

So there are no house claims here — nothing about his marriage house, his health house or his rising sign. Anyone giving you those for Yuvraj Singh is reading a noon default as though it were a birth certificate.
LESSON 07

So — is Yuvraj Singh manglik?

The most-asked astrology question about almost any famous Indian, and the honest answer is unsatisfying.

Manglik status depends entirely on which house Mars occupies — 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th. Houses need the birth minute. His isn't confirmed.

What we can say: his Mars is in Virgo, sitting with Saturn, and that much is certain at any time of that day. Whether it falls in a manglik house is not something anyone can honestly tell you — which won't stop the sites that do.
LESSON 08

How to actually read that chart square

The grid earlier on this page is a South-Indian chart, and it's the easiest of the three styles to learn because the signs never move.

Twelve boxes around the edge, one per zodiac sign, always in the same places. Pisces top-left, then clockwise: Aries, Taurus, Gemini down the right, and so on. Memorise the ring once and you can read any South-Indian chart for the rest of your life.

The planet symbols get written into whichever box they were in. That's the whole trick — a chart is just nine symbols dropped into twelve fixed boxes.

Try it: scroll back up to the chart and find the box marked VIR. Whatever symbols sit in it were in Virgo at the moment of birth. You just read a kundli.
LESSON 09

Aspects — planets shouting across the chart

A planet doesn't only affect the box it sits in. It also throws its influence at other boxes from a distance. Astrologers call this an aspect, and it's why a planet can matter for an area of life it isn't sitting in.

The basic rule: every planet aspects the box directly opposite it — seven signs away. Mars, Jupiter and Saturn each get extra reach on top of that.

His: Jupiter sits in Libra. Opposite Libra is Aries — so Jupiter influences that box from a distance, without ever sitting in it.

Why you should care: it's the usual answer to "but that planet isn't even in my career box, so why does it keep coming up?" It's shouting from across the room.
LESSON 10

Retrograde and combust, without the drama

Two words that get thrown around a lot and sound far worse than they are.

Retrograde means the planet appeared to move backwards across the sky. It isn't actually reversing — it's an optical effect of Earth overtaking it, the way a slower car seems to slide backwards when you pass it. Traditionally it makes a planet's themes more internal and slower to show results.

Combust means the planet sat very close to the Sun and was lost in its glare. The traditional reading is that its strength gets dimmed — not cancelled, dimmed.

His: Saturn, Rahu and Ketu are all retrograde in his chart. Three retrograde points sounds alarming and means very little on its own — it is a common pattern.

Neither is a disaster. Plenty of people with several retrograde planets have perfectly ordinary lives. Anyone selling you a remedy for a retrograde is selling you something.
LESSON 11

What this can and can't tell you

Worth being blunt, since this page has spent a while treating a chart as a serious object.

  • It can describe tendencies, and it can time long stretches — that part is arithmetic, and two astrologers with the same birth data will compute the same periods.
  • It can't tell you what someone will do with those tendencies. Two people with near-identical charts live completely different lives.
  • It definitely can't give exact dates for a death, a diagnosis, or an exam result — and anyone who does is guessing with confidence.
The honest framing: a chart is a description of the raw material and the weather. It is not a script, and nothing on this page should be read as one.

Quick answers

What people ask about his kundli

FAQ 01

What is Yuvraj Singh's birth time — and why won't this page use it?

The value in circulation is 12:00 noon on 12 December 1981, at PGI Chandigarh. Noon is what a record defaults to when nobody wrote the minute down, so we treat it as a placeholder rather than a birth time. That one decision is why his janam kundli here shows signs and eras but no rising sign, no houses and no manglik verdict — all three need the minute, not the day. Everything we did publish was re-run across a six-hour window and doesn't move.

FAQ 02

What is Yuvraj Singh's zodiac sign?

It depends which system is asking, which is why answers online quietly contradict each other. In Vedic astrology your rashi is your Moon sign, and his Moon is in Gemini. His Sun sits in Scorpio. A Western horoscope, which counts from a different zero point, reads the same birthday as Sagittarius. Three different words for one man, and none of them is a mistake — they're answers to different questions.

FAQ 03

What is Yuvraj Singh's nakshatra?

Ardra — the slice of Gemini his Moon landed in. A nakshatra is a finer cut than a sign: twenty-seven of them around the same circle, so it pins the Moon down far more precisely than "Gemini" manages on its own. It also does the real work on this page. Which nakshatra the Moon falls in is what sets the dasha clock — the order and the start dates of the long planetary stretches below. His stays Ardra anywhere in that six-hour window, which is the only reason we're willing to print those eras at all.

FAQ 04

What does his kundli analysis actually turn on?

One handover, in March 2012 — not a placement. His birth chart has no exalted planet, no debilitated planet and nothing in its own sign, so the sign-by-sign reading runs out almost immediately. The timing doesn't. His Jupiter stretch ran from 1996 to March 2012 and contains the debut, the six sixes and the 2011 World Cup; Saturn took over from there and contains the slower, heavier decade. Read honestly, that is a way of labelling chapters that have already happened. A dasha is a calendar, not a cause — it forecast nothing, and nothing in this chart explains his health.
